narrative:
The model has analyzed your academic situation and determined that there’s a **38% chance** you may not pass your final year. While this isn’t a certainty, it’s high enough that the school has decided you should take extra remedial courses to improve your odds. Think of it like a warning light on a dashboard—it’s telling you to pay attention and take action before things get worse.

The biggest reason for this prediction is your **history of past academic struggles**. Unlike most students who’ve never failed a class, you’ve had at least one failure before. This is the strongest signal to the model that you might be at risk of repeating that pattern. It’s not just about one bad grade—it’s a sign that you may need more support to stay on track.

Another key factor is **why you chose this school**. Most students pick their school because of the course or its reputation, but you attended primarily because it was close to home. While there’s nothing wrong with that, research shows students who are deeply invested in their education—whether through passion for the subject or a strong reputation—often perform better. Your choice suggests you might not be as engaged as you could be, which can make it harder to push through challenges.

Finally, your **aspirations for the future** play a role. Almost every student who’s doing well wants to pursue higher education, and that goal can be a powerful motivator. While you share that ambition, the model sees that without extra support, the path to success might feel harder to navigate.

The good news? You’re not alone in this. The remedial courses are designed to help you catch up, and they’ll give you the tools to turn things around. Focus on attending regularly, asking for help when you need it, and using this as a chance to build stronger study habits. The model isn’t saying you *will* fail—it’s saying you have a real opportunity to succeed if you take the right steps now.
